entries.label: 3-SAT
entries.evidence: KSatisfiability<K3> has exactly three literals per clause and returns a satisfying assignment or no solution. Each such formula is a legal instance of these board 3-SAT source definitions, which also return an assignment or NO-SOLUTION. The graph output can be recovered from one board output. This inclusion bridge does not assert that every board source instance belongs to the graph variant.

entries.label: 3-SAT
entries.evidence: These board sources ask only YES/NO for a 3-CNF formula. A satisfying assignment from graph KSatisfiability<K3> gives YES and no solution gives NO. For an at-most-three clause, use the standard polynomial fresh-variable clause-splitting gadget to obtain exact-three CNF with the same satisfiability status. This is a one-call board-to-graph reduction. The reverse direction would incorrectly demand an assignment from a decision-only board output.

entries.label: Independent Set
entries.evidence: The graph DecisionMaximumIndependentSet<SimpleGraph,One> asks whether an unweighted simple graph has an independent set of at least the input threshold. The board source takes the same graph and threshold and returns a witness or NO-SOLUTION. Its output decides the graph problem by checking whether a witness exists. This is a one-call graph-to-board reduction.

entries.label: Vertex Cover
entries.evidence: The graph DecisionMinimumVertexCover<SimpleGraph,One> asks whether an unweighted simple graph has a vertex cover of size at most the input threshold. The board source takes the same graph and threshold and returns a witness or NO-SOLUTION. Its output decides the graph problem by checking whether a witness exists. This is a one-call graph-to-board reduction.

entries.label: Triangle Partition
entries.evidence: The graph PartitionIntoTriangles model asks for a partition of a simple graph's vertices into triples inducing triangles. The board Triangle Partition source has the same witness and NO-SOLUTION outputs and accepts every graph instance of the graph model, including its divisible-by-three input restriction. The identity instance map and identity witness recovery give a one-call graph-to-board bridge.
